name: Finnish sauna
heat_source: Wood-burning or electric stove (kiuas) topped with stones
whisk_or_ritual: Water thrown on the stones for steam (löyly); birch whisk called vihta (western Finland) or vasta (eastern Finland)
headwear_note: Wool felt sauna hat (saunahattu) is used by some bathers, mostly in hotter saunas; not universal
cooling_practice: Lake or sea swim, ice-hole dip (avanto) or roll in snow in winter, cool shower, rest outdoors
unesco_status: Sauna culture in Finland - Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, inscribed 2020
notes: Many bathers settle around 80-90 °C. Humidity is low between steam bursts and jumps briefly after each ladle of water.

name: Finnish smoke sauna
heat_source: Large wood-fired stone stove with no chimney; heated for hours, smoke is vented before bathing
whisk_or_ritual: Löyly; birch whisk (vihta / vasta)
headwear_note: As in other Finnish saunas; not universal
cooling_practice: Lake swim or ice-hole dip, rest outdoors
notes: The oldest surviving Finnish sauna type. The heat is usually described as soft and long-lasting, with soot-darkened walls. Temperature left blank: published figures disagree widely.

name: Estonian sauna
heat_source: Wood-burning or electric stove (keris) with stones
whisk_or_ritual: Steam called leil; birch whisk called viht
headwear_note: Felt sauna hat (saunamüts) is common but optional
cooling_practice: Pond, lake or sea dip, snow in winter, cool shower
notes: Close relative of the Finnish sauna in build and use.

name: Estonian smoke sauna (Võromaa)
heat_source: Wood-fired stone stove with no chimney; smoke circulates in the room and is vented before bathing
whisk_or_ritual: Whisking with a viht; family customs around the sauna, including smoking meat in the sauna
headwear_note: Felt hats are used by some bathers
cooling_practice: Pond dip, rest outdoors
unesco_status: Smoke sauna tradition in Võromaa - Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, inscribed 2014
notes: A family tradition of the Võro community in southern Estonia. Temperature left blank: no reliable general range.

name: Swedish bastu
heat_source: Wood-burning or electric stove with stones
whisk_or_ritual: Water on the stones; whisks are uncommon
headwear_note: Not a traditional part of Swedish bastu; seen occasionally
cooling_practice: Lake or sea dip; seaside cold-bath houses (kallbadhus) pair a sauna with a sea plunge
notes: The word bastu is short for badstuga, 'bath cabin'.

name: Norwegian badstue
heat_source: Wood-burning or electric stove with stones
whisk_or_ritual: Water on the stones
headwear_note: Seen at public fjord saunas; not a long-standing custom
cooling_practice: Fjord, sea or lake dip
notes: Floating and harbor-side public saunas have become popular in Norwegian cities.

name: Russian banya
country_or_region: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and neighboring countries
heat_source: Large masonry or steel stove with enclosed stones; wood-fired or electric
whisk_or_ritual: Leafy whisk (venik) of birch, oak or eucalyptus used for fanning and whisking (parenie); herbal infusions on the stones
headwear_note: A wool felt banya hat is a standard part of the kit, worn dry
cooling_practice: Cold plunge pool, bucket of cold water, snow or river dip; rest and tea in the lounge room (predbannik)
notes: The steam room is called the parilka or parnaya. Cooler air than a Finnish sauna but much more steam, so it can feel hotter.

name: Russian black banya
heat_source: Wood-fired stone stove with no chimney; smoke is vented through the door or a vent before bathing
whisk_or_ritual: Venik whisking
headwear_note: Felt banya hat, as in other banyas
cooling_practice: Cold water douse, river or snow
notes: Smoke-heated counterpart of the Finnish savusauna. Temperature left blank.

name: Lithuanian pirtis
heat_source: Wood-burning stove with stones
whisk_or_ritual: Whisk called vanta (birch, oak and other plants); sessions may be led by a bath master (pirtininkas); body scrubs with salt or honey
headwear_note: Wool felt hats are widely used
cooling_practice: Pond or lake dip, cool water douse, rest between rounds
notes: Usually described as moderate heat with generous steam. Temperature left blank: published figures vary.

name: Latvian pirts
heat_source: Wood-burning stove with stones
whisk_or_ritual: Ritual led by a trained bath master (pirtnieks) using whisks (slota) of birch, oak, linden and herbs; herbal teas and scrubs
headwear_note: Wool felt hats are widely used
cooling_practice: Pond dip, cool water douse, long rests between rounds
notes: A full pirts ritual can last several hours. Temperature left blank: published figures range from about 55 °C to above 90 °C.

name: German Aufguss sauna
heat_source: Electric or wood-burning stove with stones
whisk_or_ritual: Aufguss: a sauna master pours water, often scented with essential oils, on the stones and circulates the hot air with a towel
headwear_note: Felt sauna hats (Saunahut, Saunamütze) are a common accessory
cooling_practice: Cold shower, plunge pool, fresh-air walk, then rest
notes: Saunas in German-speaking countries are typically textile-free; bathers sit on a towel. Humidity rises sharply during the Aufguss.

name: Bio sauna (soft sauna)
heat_source: Sauna stove combined with an evaporator, often with herbs
whisk_or_ritual: Herbal or aromatic vapor; sometimes colored light
cooling_practice: Cool shower and rest
notes: A gentler room between a Finnish sauna and a steam room. Sanarium is a manufacturer's trade name that is often used generically.

name: Infrared sauna
heat_source: Infrared emitters (carbon or ceramic panels) that warm the body directly
headwear_note: Optional; the air is much cooler than in a stove-heated sauna
cooling_practice: Cool shower and rest
notes: No stove, stones or steam. Usually one longer session instead of several short rounds.

name: Steam room
heat_source: Steam generator feeding a tiled, sealed room
whisk_or_ritual: Sometimes eucalyptus or other aromatics in the steam
cooling_practice: Cool shower and rest
notes: Air temperature is far lower than in a sauna, but saturated air slows the body's cooling by evaporation.

name: North American gym or club sauna
heat_source: Electric heater with stones
headwear_note: Not traditional; felt hats and towels over the head are increasingly common
cooling_practice: Cool shower; cold plunge where available
notes: Many facilities do not allow water on the heater, so these rooms often run drier than a Finnish sauna. Check posted rules.

name: Turkish hammam
country_or_region: Turkey and the former Ottoman lands
heat_source: Furnace (külhan) heating the floor, walls and water; warm marble platform (göbektaşı)
whisk_or_ritual: Scrub with a coarse mitt (kese) and a soap-foam wash, traditionally given by an attendant (tellak for men, natır for women)
headwear_note: No hat; a cotton towel is often wrapped around the head after washing. The body wrap is called a peştemal
cooling_practice: Rest in the cool room (soğukluk), often with tea
notes: Bathers move from a warm room to the hot room (sıcaklık). A visit is one long session, not timed rounds.

name: Moroccan hammam
heat_source: Wood-fired furnace heating the floors and water; a sequence of warm and hot rooms
whisk_or_ritual: Black olive-oil soap (savon beldi), scrub with a kessa glove, rhassoul clay
headwear_note: A towel may be wrapped around the hair afterward
cooling_practice: Rinse with cooler water and rest in the outer room
notes: Neighborhood public hammams remain part of weekly life. Temperature left blank.

name: Georgian sulfur bath
heat_source: Natural hot sulfur springs feeding pools under brick domes
whisk_or_ritual: Scrub with a kisi mitt and soap-foam wash by a bath attendant (mekise)
cooling_practice: Cold pool or shower, rest with tea
notes: Tbilisi takes its name from an old Georgian word for 'warm'. Water temperature left blank.

name: Roman baths (historical)
heat_source: Wood-fired furnaces with underfloor heating (hypocaust)
whisk_or_ritual: Oil rubbed on the skin and scraped off with a strigil; progression through warm (tepidarium), hot (caldarium) and cold (frigidarium) rooms
cooling_practice: Cold plunge in the frigidarium
notes: Historical entry. Some baths had a dry sweating room (laconicum). No reliable temperature figures.

name: Irish sweat house (historical)
heat_source: Turf or wood fire lit inside a small stone hut, then raked out before use
cooling_practice: Plunge in a nearby stream or pool
notes: Historical entry. Small corbelled stone huts that were in use into the 19th century. Temperatures unknown.

name: Japanese sento
heat_source: Boiler-heated water (wood, oil or gas)
whisk_or_ritual: Wash thoroughly at the seated showers before entering the shared bath
headwear_note: A small towel is often folded and placed on top of the head while soaking
cooling_practice: Cold bath (mizuburo) where available; rest in the changing room
notes: Neighborhood public bathhouse. A soaking tradition, not a sweat room; many sento also have a small sauna.

name: Japanese onsen
heat_source: Natural geothermal spring water
whisk_or_ritual: Wash before entering; towels stay out of the water
headwear_note: A small towel is often folded and placed on top of the head while soaking
cooling_practice: Rest outdoors between soaks; cool rinse
notes: Japan's Hot Springs Act defines onsen water as at least 25 °C at the source or containing specified minerals. The range given is typical bathing temperature.

name: Japanese sauna
heat_source: Electric or gas stove, usually with stones
whisk_or_ritual: Cycle of sauna, cold bath (mizuburo) and outdoor rest (gaikiyoku); some rooms offer löyly or staff-led aufguss with towel fanning
headwear_note: Sauna hats (サウナハット) in wool felt or cotton terry became popular with the recent sauna boom
cooling_practice: Cold-water bath (mizuburo), then seated rest in open air
notes: The relaxed state after repeating the cycle is called totonou.

name: Korean jjimjilbang
heat_source: Heated rooms and kilns lined with clay, salt, jade or charcoal; heated floors
whisk_or_ritual: Full-body scrub (seshin) in the wet bath area; moving between rooms of different temperatures
headwear_note: Cotton towel folded into the 'sheep head' (yangmeori) shape; a playful custom, not a heat hat
cooling_practice: Ice room, cold plunge pools in the bath area, cold drinks such as sikhye
notes: A large gender-separated bathhouse with a shared, clothed area of themed rooms. Room temperatures vary widely from mild rooms to hot kilns.

name: Korean hanjeungmak
heat_source: Domed stone or clay kiln heated by burning pine wood
whisk_or_ritual: Short stays inside the kiln, often under a protective cloth covering
headwear_note: Towels or cloth coverings over the head and shoulders
cooling_practice: Rest outside the kiln on a heated floor, cool water
notes: The traditional kiln sauna that predates the modern jjimjilbang. Temperature left blank.

name: Native American sweat lodge
heat_source: Stones heated in an outdoor fire and carried into a low, dome-shaped lodge
whisk_or_ritual: A sacred ceremony with prayer and song, conducted by a recognized leader; practices differ between nations
notes: A religious ceremony, not a recreational bath. Listed for reference only. Details are intentionally limited and temperatures are not given.

name: Temazcal
heat_source: Volcanic stones heated in a fire and brought into a low stone or adobe dome
whisk_or_ritual: Water and herbal infusions poured on the stones; ceremony guided by a temazcalero or temazcalera
cooling_practice: Cool water rinse and rest
notes: Pre-Hispanic Mesoamerican steam bath still practiced today. Temperature left blank.

name: Icelandic geothermal pool and hot tub
heat_source: Geothermally heated water
whisk_or_ritual: Thorough shower without a swimsuit before entering; hot tubs serve as a daily social meeting place
cooling_practice: Cold tub, or simply the outdoor air
unesco_status: Swimming pool culture in Iceland - Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, inscribed 2025
notes: Outdoor public pools with several hot tubs at different temperatures; many also have a sauna or steam room.
